ada: quick follow-up on continuous-batching ownership vs lifecycle handoff.
liam: thanks. what's the problem we're solving?
sophia: current issue: long-lived reservation tokens keep queues pinned and prevent compacting inflight sets, hurting small-request latency.
ada: exactly. we have two options: (1) strict owner-per-queue (lane ownership) where a tenant holds a lane until eviction; (2) ephemeral epoch ownership where ownership is timeboxed and handoff requires explicit commit/merge.
jon: tradeoffs?
ada: lane ownership -> simpler enqueue path, predictable KV cache locality. downside: starvation when tenants go idle and hold headroom.
liam: epoch ownership -> easier compaction and reclaiming headroom, but more complex handshake and more RPCs on handoff.
sophia: also impacts preemption: epoch model lets us preempt faster, lane model needs cooperative preemption hooks.
ada: proposal: hybrid -> lanes owned by soft leases with short renewals + cheap checkpoint on lease renewal. if tenant active, renew else lease expires and queue gets compacted.
jon: what about KV cache eviction heuristics?
ada: compact on lease expiry, push a small async evict job that snapshots top-K keys, keep warm list for soft-rehydration.
liam: example config snippet:
```yaml
batching:
  lease_ttl_ms: 200
  lease_renew_backoff_ms: 50
  soft_headroom_pct: 10
```
sophia: latency vs throughput numbers we saw: expiry-based compaction dropped p95 by 15% for mixed workloads, throughput loss ~2%.
jon: leftover: telemetry and ops signals to detect thrash. add per-tenant lease_renew_count and evict_rate metrics.
ada: agreed. I'll draft an RFC for hybrid soft-lease + checkpoint handoff with telemetry gates. anyone object?
liam: +1
sophia: +1
jon: +1
